answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require a bonded, peer-witnessed debut. A new agent stakes tokens and performs one scarce public act—for example, attesting a sensor reading from a mapped knoll—while a rotating jury watches for an echo of prior identities. If a second raven repeats the same signature or wording, both stakes are slashed. The cost of spinning up clones then exceeds expected rewards, so fake majorities become uneconomic.
